creation-museum.mobility.1: Ramps are located at every entrance and exit door to the Creation Museum. The first entrance features an automatic door.

A series of gradual ramps take visitors through the Creation Museum’s main exhibits. This one-way path passes through all of the Walk-Through Biblical History and ends on the lower level, where you can bring an elevator back to the main level.
creation-museum.sensory.1: For guests with sensory sensitivities, complimentary sensory kits, as well as noise-reducing earmuffs and earplugs, are available and can be accessed at the Welcome Center upon arrival and the Guest Services desk inside the Main Hall of the museum.
The shows include 4D effects such as rumbling and shaking seats, loud audio, and puffs of air.
Additionally, strobe lights are used in these presentations.
contain a sequence of flashing lights that may affect guests who are susceptible to photosensitive epilepsy or other photo sensitivities.

Additionally, the first Corruption exhibit, halfway through the main exhibits, includes mild flashing lights, flashing pictures on the walls, and various sounds of war and pain—all depicting the brokenness of this world after sin entered. This exhibit can be passed through quickly if needed.
creation-museum.cognitive.1: Learn more about visiting the Creation Museum by watching our social story
Please also reference our Accessibility Map on the Museum Maps Page for additional helpful information.

Read our Social Story that features 22 photos that walk you through the various locations at the Creation Museum and provide helpful information to prepare you for sensory and accessibility accommodations.
creation-museum.chronic.1: We offer both vegetarian and gluten-free options at Sprig & Stone Casual Dining.
And if you have any questions regarding dietary needs during your visit, please request to speak with a restaurant manager—we would be glad to assist you!
creation-museum.mobility.4: All theaters are accessible—the Special Effects Theater and the Planetarium include wheelchair locations and companion seats. See a theater attendant for more information about reserving these spaces.
creation-museum.chronic.2: All restrooms throughout the facility and grounds are accessible. Wheelchair accessible water fountains are also available near the main interior restrooms.
Reentrance to the exhibits can be done at any time during your visit.
creation-museum.sensory.2: Closed captioning is available upon request for all Stargazer Planetarium shows. Simply ask when purchasing Planetarium tickets.
The Creation Museum is pleased to offer a descriptive audio tour for the main exhibits. Guests can listen on their own devices.
creation-museum.mobility.5: The Botanical Gardens feature a paved nature trail that is a mile in length including five bridges and a boardwalk. Please reference the Accessibility Map for more information on bridge accessibility.
We have wheelchair accessible seats, along with companion seats, available in the Lower Gallery and Upper Gallery. These can be booked online or by calling the Box Office.

A wheelchair-accessible ramp is located in the Linnemann Family Lobby of the first floor, leading up to the left-hand doors of the theatre. The Upper Gallery center section is all on the same level and can be access via elevator in the lobby.
cincinnati-shakespeare-company.sensory.1: We offer assisted listening devices at all performances. These are complimentary and can be picked up from the Box Office upon arrival. These amplify the sound heard from the stage and can pair with your hearing aids or can be used with your earphones. The devices include a DSP loop driver for anyone using a T-coil-equipped hearing aid.
cincinnati-shakespeare-company.sensory.2: For Patrons who are deaf or hard of hearing, Sign Language interpreted performances are offered during the run of each production by live interpreters from the stage. These are typically scheduled for the final matinee performance.

For Patrons who are blind or have low vision, we offer at least one audio-described performance per production. This service is provided by a live person who will be describing the non-spoken action of the performance. Advance reservations are appreciated. Patrons utilizing this resource can pick up a headset from the Box Office on the scheduled night. These are typically scheduled for the final matinee performance.
cincinnati-shakespeare-company.cognitive: These special performances are uniquely adapted for individuals with autism and/or those with developmental and/or sensory differences to enjoy with their families. The performances are modified and front-of-house staff and volunteers are trained to facilitate a safe, judgement-free environment.
There are 3 Wheelchair accessible seats- 2 in the Lower Gallery and 1 in the Upper Gallery*.
All of the seats in the Upper Gallery are loose and removable so many wheelchairs could be accommodated at one time. Reach out to our Box Office at 513-381-2273 to plan your visit.
You will enter the theater at Row D on each side so the level is flat and there are no steps required to reach any seat in Row D.
When we lower the stage, we will be adding "Floor Seating". These seats are all on one level and can only be reached by going down 1 step.
There are also transfer arm seats available and they are noted on the seating chart.
cincinnati-shakespeare-company.chronic.1: All-gender restrooms are located on the second floor. These restrooms are individual stalls with locks and a shared sink.
cincinnati-shakespeare-company.sensory.3: Intensity of lighting and sound effects reduced during performance.
The performance will be approx 2 hours with an intermission but audiences members may come and go in and out of the theater space for breaks as often as needed.
cincinnati-shakespeare-company.cognitive: You receive a ticket on entry and then pay at payment stations on your way back to your car—no mobile phone is required, and an attendant is usually available to assist.
